title: How do we name three large products in both systems?
description: Three products are found by setting aside the zeros at the end, multiplying the other digits and putting the zeros back. Each answer is then cut into groups and named in the Indian and the American systems. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking the second product is one hundred forty seven crore.
teaching_notes: One idea: set aside the zeros, multiply the other digits, put the zeros back, and then cut into groups to name the number in each system. Ask the class how many zeros the answer will end with before any multiplying is done. Watch for students who count the zeros wrongly and name the number a crore too big.

source: 1250 × 380, 2100 × 70,000, 6400 × 62,500: Calculate the product and read the number in both Indian and American naming systems.
video_script.why: The child has used shortcuts to multiply by tens and hundreds, and now finds products of large numbers and names them in both systems.
video_script.substitution: Set aside the zeros at the end, multiply the other digits, put the zeros back, and cut the digits into Indian groups and American groups.
video_script.anchor: Three products written in a column: 1250 × 380, 2100 × 70,000 and 6400 × 62,500, with a box for the Indian name and a box for the American name beside each.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads 21 × 7 = 147 and the zeros as one hundred forty seven crore. The product 147 followed by 6 zeros has 9 digits, but 147 crore would need 10 digits.
video_script.payoff_line: Each product is named in both systems

final_answer.spoken: four lakh seventy five thousand, fourteen crore seventy lakh, and forty crore

never_show: the second product or its names before the answer beat
maths_rules: 2100 × 70,000 = (21 × 7) × (100 × 10,000) = 147 with 6 zeros = 14,70,00,000: Indian 14 crore 70 lakh, American 147 million
Indian groups: 3 digits from the right then 2s; American groups: 3s
a crore has 7 zeros, so 147 crore has 10 digits, but 147 with 6 zeros has 9
video_script.design: One idea: set aside zeros, multiply, put zeros back, then cut into groups to name. Wrong idea: Keeko says one hundred forty seven crore. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.
open_questions: The songs per year and the Earth to Sun distance follow-up questions in the book are not covered in this video.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, set aside one zero from each number of the first product.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred twenty five times thirty eight is five thousand minus two hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is four thousand seven hundred fifty, and two zeros go back at the end.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 2100 × 70,000: set aside 2 zeros and 4 zeros; 21 × 7 = 147; 147 with 6 zeros back

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, set aside two zeros from twenty one hundred, and four zeros from seventy thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty one times seven is one hundred forty seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Six zeros go back at the end of one hundred forty seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 6400 × 62,500: set aside 2 zeros from each; 64 × 625 = 16 × 4 × 625 = 16 × 2500 = 40,000; put 4 zeros back

marks.m1: two zeros slide off 6400 and two zeros slide off 62,500

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, set aside two zeros from each number of the third product.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Sixty four times six hundred twenty five is sixteen times two thousand five hundred, which is forty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Four zeros go back at the end of forty thousand.
